name: Creepage & Clearance
blurb: minimum conductor spacing for a working voltage per IPC-2221, as a table
intro: The minimum spacing between two conductors at a given voltage, from IPC-2221B table 6-1, for every location (internal, external bare, under mask, coated, component leads) and altitude. It checks your gap against it; it is functional spacing, not a safety-agency creepage rating.

inputs.label: Where the conductors are
options: B4 External, under solder mask / polymer

inputs.label: Your spacing (to check)
inputs.help: Optional: the gap you have on the board.

examples.title: 230 V AC mains traces on the outer layer
400 V DC bus on an inner layer

usage: Give the voltage between two conductors in volts, whether it is DC/peak ('dc') or AC RMS ('rms'), and the IPC-2221 location column (B1, B2, B3, B4, A5, A6, A7); optionally your actual gap in mm. Returns the minimum spacing in mm and mil, pass/fail for your gap, the spacing for all columns at that voltage and the whole table 6-1. For mains or safety isolation also apply IEC 62368-1 / IEC 60664-1, which usually ask for more.
sources: IPC-2221B Generic Standard on Printed Board Design, section 6.3 and table 6-1 (electrical conductor spacing)
IEC 60664-1 / IEC 62368-1 for safety creepage and clearance (not computed here)
